title: Cash Debit or Credit: Which is best?
summary: Public service episode comparing cash, credit cards, and debit cards. Hosts open with a news item about Lorie Black, a Massachusetts Black Friday mercenary who shops in line for others, then weigh anonymity and proof of ownership of cash, fraud liability protections under the Fair Credit Billing Act and Electronic Fund Transfer Act, PIN security, fees and interest rates, overdraft fee rules, the pain of paying, rewards programs, and building credit history. They also discuss proposals to replace dollar bills with dollar coins. The episode ends with a listener mail about Johnny Eck, and thank-yous and contact information.

segments.title: Opening and disclaimer
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the public service episode, disclaim being financial advisers, and preview the cash, credit, and debit comparison.

segments.title: Lorie Black, Black Friday mercenary
segments.summary: News item about Lorie Black, a thirty-two-year-old preschool teacher from Auburn, Massachusetts, who has attended fifteen Black Fridays and offers to shop in line for others via Craigslist. The hosts discuss what payment method she should use.

segments.title: Anonymity, proof of ownership, and signatures
segments.summary: Cash is anonymous and untracked, while cards create records useful for budgeting. Cash cannot prove ownership once lost. Discussion of signing cards, writing 'see ID' on the back, and signature verification.

segments.title: Fraud liability protections
segments.summary: Credit cards are covered under the Fair Credit Billing Act and debit cards under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act. Liability is capped at fifty dollars, and debit liability rises to five dollars if reported within two days of noticing the loss.

segments.title: PIN security and card tracking
segments.summary: Debit cards have a PIN that adds security, while credit cards do not use PINs. Purchases on cards can be tracked by law enforcement and others.

segments.title: Fees, interest rates, and debt statistics
segments.summary: Credit cards carry interest and financing fees, with average rates near fourteen percent and average credit card debt around sixteen thousand dollars. Statistics on card ownership, oldest obligations, and total consumer debt are discussed. Paying the full balance monthly, as with American Express, avoids finance charges.

segments.title: Overdraft fees and debit card fees
segments.summary: Debit cards are generally fee-free, but overdraft fees were limited by a rule requiring customers to opt in. Bank of America's proposed debit card monthly fee was rolled back, while Wells Fargo was reported to still plan one. Discussion of the posting-order scandal.

segments.title: Pain of paying, rewards, and credit history
segments.summary: Cash makes spending feel real, while cards make it easier to overspend. Credit cards offer rewards such as miles and cash back and help build the credit history needed for loans.

segments.title: Dollar bills versus dollar coins
segments.summary: Super Committee proposal to phase out dollar bills for dollar coins, which cost more to make but last three times longer. Mention of Crane and Co, the maker of currency paper.

segments.title: Wrap-up of the comparison
segments.summary: Hosts recap the tradeoffs and advise listeners to choose the payment method that suits them, noting that it is fine to pay in cash occasionally.

segments.title: Listener mail: Johnny Eck and thank-yous
segments.summary: A listener's mother mentions Johnny Eck, the half-man sideshow performer, who lived at the listener's grandfather's house. Hosts also thank Little Bit Sweets for candy, Scumbag Movies for DVDs, and share contact information.
